text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 0.33% today to $388.38, extending a sharp 2-week decline of 2.77% from highs near $425. The stock has been under pressure as crude oil prices whipsawed—US oil closed today at $96.41 a barrel, down significantly from levels above $100 just days ago—and market uncertainty around Iran's regional conflict and potential US policy responses (including a proposed diesel export ban) has kept energy investors on edge. Refineries are running at 94% capacity with healthy product inventories, so the weakness appears driven by crude price volatility rather than operational stress.

The broader headwind is simple: refiners like Marathon make money by processing cheap crude into fuel products, so falling oil prices compress those margins. Geopolitical risk remains elevated—Iran talks offer diplomatic hope but also create uncertainty about whether tensions will truly ease or escalate, making it hard for the market to price in a durable direction for crude. This ambiguity has knocked the stock lower over the past week.
